CLINICAL INDICATION:
Groin pain / palpable bulge; rule out inguinal hernia.
TECHNIQUE:

High-frequency linear (7–15 MHz) grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound of the bilateral inguinal canals, Hesselbach triangles, and femoral canals was performed at rest and during dynamic Valsalva maneuvers in both supine and upright/standing positions.
FINDINGS:
Right Inguinal Region:

Hernia Type & Location: No hernia. The right inferior epigastric artery is clearly identified. No fascial defect or abnormal protrusion of peritoneal fat or bowel is seen either medial (Hesselbach triangle) or lateral (deep inguinal ring) to the inferior epigastric vessels at rest or during provocative Valsalva maneuvers in supine and standing positions.
Fascial Defect & Sac: No fascial defect or hernia sac.
Reducibility & Viability: Not applicable (no hernia identified).
Scrotal / Labial Extension: No inguinoscrotal extension.
Left Inguinal Region:
Hernia Type & Location: Normal left inguinal canal and Hesselbach triangle with no fascial defect or hernia sac at rest or with Valsalva.
Fascial Defect & Sac: No fascial defect or hernia sac.
Reducibility & Viability: Not applicable (no hernia identified).
Scrotal / Labial Extension: No inguinoscrotal extension.
Soft Tissues & Lymph Nodes:
Scattered normal-appearing, oval reactive inguinal lymph nodes with preserved fatty hila measuring up to 1.1 cm in long axis. No soft tissue mass or fluid collection.
IMPRESSION:
No sonographic evidence of a right or left inguinal hernia at rest or during provocative Valsalva maneuvers.

subs.title: Indirect Inguinal Hernia (Reducible)
items: Originating lateral to the inferior epigastric artery at the deep inguinal ring, there is a fascial defect measuring [X.X] cm through which a hernia sac measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm protrudes anteromedially along the inguinal canal during Valsalva/standing, containing [omental fat / a loop of viable small bowel]. The hernia contents completely reduce at rest in the supine position.

subs.title: Indirect Inguinal Hernia with Inguinoscrotal Extension
items: A large indirect inguinal hernia originates lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels (neck width [X.X] cm) and extends inferiorly through the superficial inguinal ring into the [right / left] hemiscrotum, measuring [X.X] cm in craniocaudal length and containing [omental fat and multiple loops of peristalsing small bowel]. Both testes remain normal in size and Doppler vascularity.

subs.title: Direct Inguinal Hernia (Reducible)
items: Originating medial to the inferior epigastric artery within Hesselbach triangle, there is an anterior protrusion through a weakened transversalis fascia / defect measuring [X.X] cm in width, creating a broad-based hernia sac measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm containing [extraperitoneal fat / bowel] during Valsalva. The hernia reduces completely upon relaxation.

subs.title: Cord Lipoma (Important Mimic)
items: Within the [right / left] inguinal canal adjacent to the spermatic cord, there is an elongated, well-circumscribed, homogeneously hyperechoic fat-containing mass measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm that moves slightly with cord traction/Valsalva but demonstrates no continuity with the peritoneal cavity or fascial defect, consistent with a spermatic cord lipoma.

subs.title: Strangulated Groin Hernia (Surgical Emergency)
items: Strangulation Alert: Within the [right / left] [indirect inguinal / direct inguinal / femoral] hernia sac, there is a fixed, non-reducible loop of fluid-distended, thick-walled small bowel (wall thickness [X.X] mm) accompanied by anechoic/complex fluid within the hernia sac and absent intramural color Doppler blood flow, diagnostic of a strangulated hernia.

subs.title: Post-Herniorrhaphy Mesh Evaluation (Normal)
items: Echogenic linear surgical mesh is visualized intact along the posterior inguinal wall with mild surrounding postoperative scar tissue; no recurrent fascial defect, hernia protrusion, or periprosthetic fluid collection/seroma is identified.

bank.title: PART 2: EXAMPLE FINDINGS FROM THE SAMPLE ABNORMAL REPORT
items: Inferior Epigastric Vessels & Inguinal Canal: At the site of palpable right groin swelling, there is a fascial defect measuring 1.8 cm in width originating lateral to the inferior epigastric artery at the deep inguinal ring and extending anteromedially along the inguinal canal toward the superficial ring, consistent with a right indirect inguinal hernia.

Contents, Size & Reducibility: Upon Valsalva and standing, a hernia sac measuring 4.8 x 2.4 x 2.0 cm protrudes through the canal, containing omental fat and a loop of non-dilated small bowel. The contents completely reduce spontaneously upon relaxation in the supine position. Visualized small bowel demonstrates normal wall thickness (2.1 mm), active peristalsis, and preserved color Doppler flow. No free fluid within the hernia sac.
Right indirect inguinal hernia (neck width 1.8 cm, sac 4.8 cm) containing reducible omental fat and viable small bowel, without signs of incarceration or strangulation.

bank.title: PART 3: NORMAL PHRASES
items: Inferior Epigastric Vessels & Inguinal Canal: The right inferior epigastric artery is clearly identified. Inferior Epigastric Vessels & Inguinal Canal: Normal left inguinal canal and Hesselbach triangle with no fascial defect or hernia sac at rest or with Valsalva.
Scattered normal-appearing, oval reactive inguinal lymph nodes with preserved fatty hila measuring up to 1.1 cm in long axis. No soft tissue mass or fluid collection.
No sonographic evidence of a right or left inguinal hernia at rest or during provocative Valsalva maneuvers.
